title: Recency-Based Confidence Scoring Bug Fix
description: Discovered that async_prep.py was calling calculate_confidence_level(category, level) instead of calculate_confidence_level(entry_age_minutes). Fixed by updating all three entry types (OperatorIntention, ResearchTopic, DecisionPoint) to use recency parameter. Tool now correctly outputs ~95% [HIGH CONFIDENCE] for fresh entries (age 0 min), matching design spec.

Concurrent stress testing validates BB capacity under realistic load. 16 agents × 20 entries = 320 total writes achieved P99 1.195ms with zero errors — system exceeds SLA requirements comfortably. This is the signal we needed before production deployment of async_prep.py.
implications: System has headroom for async_prep integration
Can proceed to quiet window deployment without scaling concerns
P99 latency well below human-perceptible thresholds

description: Stress test results serve operator decision-making: can Creator trust Blackboard won't become bottleneck when async prep goes live? Metrics artifact = external-subject compliant because it answers 'when should I deploy?' not 'how am I doing?'
